question.text: Skyvault Ventures (Cat I AIF — Angel Fund) is investing INR 15 crore in a DPIIT-recognised startup at a subscription price higher than the independent valuer's DCF fair value. Historically, this triggered 'Angel Tax' concerns. What is the position under the Finance Act 2024 with effect from 1 April 2025?

answer.text: Angel tax (Section 56(2)(viib)) has been ABOLISHED with effect from 1 April 2025, eliminating this tax risk for the investee company.
Angel tax continues to apply at a 30% rate at investor level.
Angel tax only applies to non-resident investors now.
Angel tax has been increased to 40% from FA 2024.

explanation.text: The Logic: The Finance (No.2) Act 2024 REPEALED Section 56(2)(viib) — the so-called 'angel tax' — with effect from assessment year 2025-26 (i.e., transactions on or after 1 April 2025). Previously, if a closely-held company issued shares at a premium exceeding FMV, the excess was taxable in the company's hands as 'income from other sources'. The abolition simplifies capital raising for startups and is particularly helpful for Cat I Angel Funds and Cat II VC funds. The Trap: Option B retains the abolished regime. Option C invents an NR-only version. Option D claims a rate hike that did not happen — the provision was scrapped entirely. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C flags this as a major post-Budget 2024 update. XIX-A will update distributor training. X-A/X-B (IA) note it for client startup advisory. Note: pre-FA 2024 valuations for transactions BEFORE 1 April 2025 may still be under litigation — GAAR remains an overlay concern even post-repeal. Manager's Pro-Tip: For Cat I Angel Funds, this repeal removes one big investee-company-level objection during negotiation. But you still need valuation defensibility for accounting, SEBI reporting, and GAAR — commission a Merchant-Banker DCF + comparables and document the commercial rationale in the IC memo.
